questions.text: Common channel signaling provides that
options: Control equipment of switching centers exchange signaling information in packet switching
Each channel dedicated to user data transmission is associated with a different channel for signaling
Signaling between switching centers occurs by sharing a single satellite channel
questions.hint: In the common channel signaling the user information travels on separate channels but with a single signaling channel used to control the reporting of all user channels. The channel signaling works in packet.

questions.text: The characteristics of a fully connected mesh topology are
options: High number of channels, good fault tolerance, easy routing
High number of channels, good fault tolerance, difficult routing
Low number of channels, bad fault tolerance, difficult routing
questions.hint: See slides "Knitted topology". There is always a way in the fully connected mesh direct between each node.

questions.text: Conversational interactive telecommunication services are characterized by
options: Low probability of error in the transfer of information
Transfer of information in real time
Storage of information on the network and delivery to the recipient in a deferred time
questions.hint: In conversational interactive services, communication takes place with the transfer of extreme to extreme information in real time. See slides “Conversational Interactive Services”.

questions.text: In packet-switched networks the factors that lead to the choice of small packets dimensions are
options: Lower impact of control information, higher efficiency in the transfer of big SDUs
Better chance of parallelization, less transfer delay, less chance of bit error
Better chance of parallelization, less delay in packaging, less probability of package error
questions.hint: Short packets favor transmission in parallel on different channels of packets of the same communication, short packets reduce the delay of packetization, long packets reduce the percentage of control information.

questions.text: In the OSI model, the transport layer provides services
options: Building on services from the application layer
Relying on the services provided by the network layer
Relying on the services provided by the session level
questions.hint: Think of the ISO / OSI stack. See slides on the OSI model.

questions.text: Which of the following statements conforms to the ISO / OSI reference model?
options: An (N)-entity and an (N-1)-entity can have the same address
One (N)-entity can be associated with two different (N-1)-addresses
Two (N)-entities can be associated with the same (N-1)-address
questions.hint: Each entity is characterized by the abbreviation (address) of its own layer, so A and C are wrong and by exclusion the correct answer is B. Internet source.

questions.text: In a Go-Back-N windowed protocol it may be convenient to increase the size of the transmission window
options: When the transmission speed increases at the same size of the data units and the same delays
When the transmission speed decreases at the same size of the data units and the same delays
When the distance between transmitter and receiver decreases
When the probability of channel error increases
questions.hint: Efficiency of a window protocol. Wt = k*(1 + 2*(tp/tx)). As the transmission speed increases, tx decreases, requiring Wt to increase to maintain efficiency.

questions.text: A Go-Back-N windowed protocol does not require an increase in complexity compared to Stop-And-Wait in relation to
options: Amount of memory required by the transmitter
Minimum amount of sequence numbers required to distinguish data units
Amount of memory required at the receiver
questions.hint: The Go-Back-N does not require an increase in complexity compared to the receiver window of Stop-And-Wait.

questions.text: The Aloha and S-Aloha protocols
options: To avoid interference between transmissions of users sharing a broadcast channel, assign each user a predetermined time interval in which to transmit

Do not implement any preventive control to avoid interference between transmissions of users sharing a broadcast channel; only in case of interference (collision) do they intervene, repeating transmission after a fixed delay

Do not implement any preventive control to avoid interference between transmissions of users sharing a broadcast channel; only in case of interference (collision) do they intervene, repeating transmission after a random delay
questions.hint: Aloha has low efficiency because nodes transmit without coordination. Collisions trigger random backoff.

questions.text: The architecture of the Internet protocols is organized
options: In seven levels
In four levels
In six levels
In a completely non-layered way
questions.hint: Review the concepts related to General Networking.

questions.text: The TCP receiver
options: Send cumulative acknowledgments (ACKs)
Sends an acknowledgment (ACK) for each segment
Does not send feedback
questions.hint: TCP uses window protocols with cumulative ACKs.

questions.text: The header of the TCP segment
options: Always fixed size of 20 bytes
Variable size depending on options
Fixed size of 40 bytes
questions.hint: TCP header contains an options field of variable size. See slides "TCP".

questions.text: The logical addresses on the Internet are
options: Determinants free from subnet admins
Organized in domains
Completely free format
questions.hint: See slides on IP.

questions.text: The routing protocol can be used between ASs (Autonomous Systems)
options: EGP (Exterior Gateway Protocol)
RIP (Routing Information Protocol)
OSPF (Open Shortest Path First)
questions.hint: Routers of different AS exchange information via EGP.

questions.text: In the OSI model, a (N)-connection
options: Can be realized through one or more (N-1) connections
Terminated by two (N-1)-CEPs
Realized through one or more (N+1)-connections
Only through multiple (N-1) connections
questions.hint: By definition, (N) layer provides services to (N+1) layer.

questions.text: Compared to the 10 Mbit/s Ethernet standard, 100 Mbit/s Ethernet MAC protocol
options: Modified for more efficient collision detection
Modified to avoid collisions, improve performance, support real-time
Unchanged, accepts reduction of “collision domain”
Unchanged, maximum size unchanged
questions.hint: See slides on MAC.

questions.text: The metric (cost) in a routing algorithm
options: Expresses the weight of a link in path selection
Expresses computational complexity
Expresses probability shortest path used
questions.hint: See slides.

questions.text: Advantages of virtual circuit services over datagram services
options: Less packet delay, routing calculation for each packet
Less variability of delays, maintain sequence, routing for each packet
Less variability of delays, maintain sequence, routing only when opening connection
questions.hint: Virtual circuit maintains sequence, less delay variation, routing only at connection open.

questions.text: IEEE 802.1d Transparent Bridges
options: Routing follows "backward learning" and flooding
Routing based on exchange of routing tables
Routing always occurs in flooding mode
questions.hint: Internet source.

questions.text: Compared to Fast Ethernet at 100 Mb/s, 1 Gb/s Ethernet respects collision recognition
options: Decreasing distance between nodes
Using optical fiber
Increasing minimum size of PDUs
questions.hint: Larger PDUs required to maintain Transmission > RTT.

questions.text: Compared to CBR, VBR sources
options: Greater difference between max and min transmission speed
More stringent max delay requirements
More stringent average delay requirements
questions.hint: VBR used for streaming; CBR for videoconferencing.

questions.text: End-to-end error recovery in Internet environment, when present:
options: Is always performed only by application processes
Is performed at the Transport layer
Is performed at the Internet (network) layer
Is not provided for any type of service
questions.hint: End-to-end principle applies at transport layer for TCP/UDP.

questions.text: The POP3 protocol
options: Used for blocking pop-ups
Used for email exchange between servers
Used to transfer email from server to client
Uses encrypted authentication
questions.hint: POP3 is client-server protocol for email access.

questions.text: Collision domain in Ethernet
options: Portion of network where same collision is detected
Number of bits in packet header damaged by collision
Set of nodes interrupting transmission due to collision
questions.hint: See slides “Domain of collision”.

questions.text: In an IP subnet
options: Hosts share same network prefix
Network prefix is first 3 bytes of address
questions.hint: All subnets must share the same network address.

questions.text: OSI reference model: (N)-PCI can contain
options: (N)-addresses
(N+1)-addresses
(N-1)-addresses
questions.hint: N-level header contains N addresses; N-SDU contains (N+1) addresses.

questions.text: The TCP protocol
options: Provides error detection on data of each segment through a checksum
Provides error detection only on the segment header
Does not provide error detection and recovery on data
questions.hint: TCP offers checksum on received packets.

questions.text: P/F bit in LAPB
options: Implicit confirmation
Request confirmation from receiver
Speeds up transmission
questions.hint: Poll/Final field single bit: Poll for request, Final for response.

questions.text: Protocols not performing data unit delimitation
options: LAPB (ISDN B channel)
LaPF (Frame Relay)
PPP
IEEE 802.2 LLC
questions.hint: Delimiters inserted by MAC protocol.

questions.text: Ethernet full-duplex mode requires
options: The ability to receive and transmit packets simultaneously
The availability of fault protection techniques through two disjoint paths between each pair of nodes
Full support for both 10 Mbit/s and 100 Mbit/s speeds
questions.hint: Full-duplex uses separate cables for TX/RX.

questions.text: Tree topology characteristics
options: Low channels, bad fault tolerance, easy routing
Low channels, good fault tolerance, easy routing
High channels, good fault tolerance, difficult routing
questions.hint: See slides "Tree topology".

questions.text: IPv4 addresses are:
options: Of fixed total length, composed of a variable-length part that identifies the network and a variable-length part that identifies the host
Of fixed total length, composed of a fixed-length part that identifies the network and a fixed-length part tha tidentifies the host
Of variable length, composed of a variable-length part that identifies the network and a variable-length part that identifies the host
questions.hint: IPV4 definition.

questions.text: Store-and-forward large PDUs
options: Decreases probability of bit errors
Minimizes transfer delay
Requires larger header
Increases overall transfer delay
questions.hint: Large packets delay transmission; small packets preferred.

questions.text: Selective Repeat protocol Wt/Wr
options: Works only if Wt + Wr <= 2^k
Only if Wt <= 2^k
Only if Wr <= 2^k
questions.hint: See “Selective Repeat” slides.

questions.text: Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP)
options: Go-Back-N for loss recovery
Use address field to distinguish commands
Uses 01111110 sequence to delimit data
questions.hint: See slides “Encapsulating PPP PDUs”.

questions.text: Store-and-forward advantages
options: Different speeds between channels on same switch
Reduce delays through switching node
Reduce packet header size
Use Forward Error Correction
questions.hint: Ability to adapt to channels with different capacities.

questions.text: The difference between teleservices, bearer services and supplementary services lies in the fact that:
options: While bearer services offer only information transfer between user-network interfaces, teleservices involve user equipment functions according to predetermined protocols; supplementary services instead modify or integrate a bearer service and a teleservice

While teleservices offer only information transfer between user-network interfaces, bearer services involve user equipment functions according to predetermined protocols; supplementary services are special services for data transfer

While bearer services offer only information transfer between user-network interfaces, teleservices involve user equipment functions according to predetermined protocols; supplementary services are special services for data transfer
questions.hint: Bearer services are essential; teleservices rely on them.

questions.text: OSI model functions in telecom network
options: Operations on service interface
Rules between entities in same layer
Operations within architectural layer
questions.hint: B defines protocol.

questions.text: Consider a transmitting host that uses the TCP protocol and a receiver at infinite speed, i.e., that always declares the maximum available value as the reception window. Given a current window at the transmitter of size equal to 10 segments, with a maximum receiver window equal to 20 segments, at the moment when the transmitter receives a segment containing an ACK from the receiver, which of the following situations is possible?
options: Current window becomes 3 segments
Current window becomes 51 segments
Current window becomes 11 segments
Current window becomes 13 segments
questions.hint: Slow-start, cwnd increases +1 segment per ACK.

questions.text: Domain Name System (DNS)
options: Assign Ethernet address from IP
Map (3)-addresses to (2)-addresses
Know IP of logical name website
Know physical location of host
questions.hint: DNS maps logical names to IP addresses.

questions.text: Given a number of nodes and a number of channels, a topology T1 for which the average distance between nodes is smaller than another topology T2, in the presence of uniformly distributed traffic:
options: Allows handling the same amount of traffic on the channels
Allows handling a lower amount of traffic on the channels
Allows handling a greater amount of traffic on the channels
questions.hint: Throughput inversely proportional to average distance.

questions.text: The piggybacking technique in window protocols consists in the possibility of:
options: Sending back to the transmitter any data units that have suffered transmission errors
Concatenating multiple acknowledgments in a data unit
Carrying acknowledgment information and user data in the same data unit
Having the receiver explicitly signal to the transmitter any data unit losses
questions.hint: Piggybacking allows ACK info in opposite-direction PDU.

questions.text: Distinguishing commands and responses in layer 2 LaPB protocol frames has the purpose of:
options: Understanding whether a Poll bit or a Final bit was sent
Understanding who is the recipient of the frame
Distinguishing supervision frames from information frames
questions.hint: LAPB frame: supervision field for control only.

questions.text: LAN bus topology CSMA
options: Time detection greater at ends, less at center
Same for all nodes
Depends on position relative to transmitters
questions.hint: See slides "CSMA".

questions.text: Header of packet in datagram service
options: Source & destination addresses
Destination + connection ID
Connection ID
Source + connection ID
questions.hint: See slides “IP datagram format”.

questions.text: Compared to the 10 Mbit/s Ethernet standard, in the definition of 100 Mbit/s Ethernet, the MAC protocol
options: Has been modified by introducing a collision avoidance mechanism, which allows improving performance and supporting real-time services
Has been kept unchanged, accepting the reduction by a factor of ten (approximately) of the maximum size of the "collision domain"
Has been kept unchanged, maintaining the maximum size of the "collision domain" unchanged, but increasing the minimum frame size by a factor of ten
Has been modified to allow more efficient collision detection
questions.hint: See transparencies.

questions.text: PPP duplicate quiz
options: Makes use of a go-back-n window protocol for recovery of data unit losses
Makes use of the address field in data units to distinguish those sent by the user from those sent by the operator
Makes use of a known bit sequence to delimit data units
questions.hint: See transparencies “Encapsulating PPP PDUs”.

questions.text: IP router after calculating route
options: Change source & destination IP
Edit TTL & checksum
Edit TTL only
questions.hint: TTL changes require checksum update.

questions.text: An Ethernet card in a switch processes (that is, it reads and decides whether and how to route)
options: Only packets with broadcast destination MAC address
All packets, regardless of the destination address
Only packets with unicast destination MAC address equal to that of the switch
Only packets with multicast destination MAC address
questions.hint: See switch operation.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true? A host connected to the Internet, at the moment when it wants to transmit/receive data to/from any other host on the Internet network, must know. where he wants to transmit / receive data to / from any other host on the Internet, he must know
options: Its own IP address and related mask, its own MAC address, the IP address of the default router, the IP address of a DNS
Only its own MAC address
Only its own IP address
questions.hint: Fonte Marchetto.

questions.text: By commutation we mean
options: The exchange of information concerning the control and management of a telecommunications network
The transfer of information from one point to one or more other points
The process of interconnecting resources for the time necessary for communication
questions.hint: See transparencies “Function: switching”. The C represents the 7 circuit switching! There control information.

questions.text: In the OSI model, the transport layer provides services
options: Building on services from the application layer
Relying on the services provided by the network layer
Relying on the services provided by the session level
questions.hint: Review the concepts related to Transport Layer.

questions.text: In the OSI model, the network layer provides services
options: Building on the services provided by the application layer
Based on the services provided by the transport layer
Relying on the services provided by the link layer
questions.hint: The network layer is above the connection layer.

questions.text: In a real mobile radio channel, the fading phenomenon consists in:
options: Decrease in received power, caused by the distance between transmitter and receiver
Rapid variation of the received power, caused by sources operating at the same frequency
Reduction of the received power, caused by atmospheric sources such as rain and snow
Rapid variation of the received power, caused by the presence of moving obstacles
questions.hint: See slides “Real (mobile) radio channel”.

questions.text: In the IP header, or in the PCI of the IP protocol, they are mandatory contents:
options: The IP address of a source and destination
The port of a source and destination
The Window field that allows the receiver to report the current size of the window reception to the transmitter
questions.hint: See slides “IP datagram format”.

questions.text: The IP protocol:
options: Guarantees error detection only on the datagram header
Guarantees error detection on the header and the content of the datagram
It does not provide any kind of error protection
Guarantees error detection only on the content of the datagram
questions.hint: The Header Checksum field (16 bits) is used to verify that the IP header has arrived intact at destination. It only checks the integrity of the header.

questions.text: The Go-Back-N protocol is more complex than the Stop-And-Wait protocol due
options: The greater complexity of the transmitter
The greater complexity of the receiver
The greater complexity of both the receiver and the transmitter
questions.hint: Complexity at the receiver is nearly the same; the transmitter is more complex due to window >1.

questions.text: The use of cookies in the HTTP protocol allows you to
options: Associate multiple requests made by the same browser or user
Cache the responses received
Download all the objects contained in a page by opening a single TCP connection
Send the response to the client using different fragments (Chunked Transfer)
questions.hint: See slides "cookies".

questions.text: In a fully connected mesh topology with N nodes, the number of channels bidirectional is equal to
options: 2N
No.
questions.hint: See slides “Knitted topology”.

questions.text: The IP protocol provides a service
options: Unreliable (i.e. no delivery guarantee) and connectionless
Reliable (i.e. with delivery guarantee) and connectionless
Unreliable (i.e. without delivery guarantee) and connection oriented
questions.hint: IP is connectionless and best-effort; no guarantees.

questions.text: Compared to the IP protocol, the UDP protocol
options: It adds nothing
Adds the ability to carry messages by distinguishing between different application processes on the same host
It allows a reliable transport of information
questions.hint: UDP is unreliable; it provides multiplexing and demultiplexing.

questions.text: Which of the following line encodings is more efficient, i.e., requires physically lower bit rate at the same rate of information transmitted?
options: 4B5B encoding
64B66B encoding
8B10B encoding
questions.hint: 64B66B requires a minimal increase in physical bit rate (1.03×) versus 1.25× for 4B5B or 8B10B.

questions.text: The CIDR (Classless Inter Domain Routing), based on the use of netmasks in IP, is a technique used in order to
options: Decrease the convergence time of routing protocols
Efficiently use the IP addressing space
Avoid the formation of routing loops in routing
questions.hint: See transparencies.

questions.text: The DSL access network separates data and voice on the same transmission medium between the devices user and control panel devices using:
options: Time multiplexing
Multiple access to frequency division
Multiple access to time division
Frequency multiplexing
questions.hint: ADSL uses frequency division with filters at user and central side.

questions.text: The Stop-And-Wait protocol
options: It can only work using more than one numbering bit
It can work using a number of numbering bits greater than or equal to 1
It can only work using a single numbering bit
It can only work using fewer numbering bits than the window size transmission
questions.hint: Using ≥1 bit reduces malfunctions and allows PDU/ACK tracking.

questions.text: In a tree topology with N nodes, the number of bidirectional channels is equal to
options: N
2N
questions.hint: See slides “Tree Topology”.

questions.text: In the UDP header, or in the PCI of the UDP protocol, are mandatory contents
options: The value of the Maximum Segment Size negotiated between transmitter and receiver
The checksum field, for error detection
Some flags (in the CODE field) for opening and closing the connection
questions.hint: UDP provides multiplexing and checksum error checking.

questions.text: The transport layer on the Internet
options: Provides reliable information transport if UDP protocol is used
It only provides unreliable transportation
Always provides reliable information transport
Provides reliable information transport if using the TCP protocol
questions.hint: TCP provides reliable transport; UDP does not.

questions.text: In a routing table of an IP router there is a mask in which the first 24 bits (the most significant) are 1 and the last 8 bits (the least significant) are 0. Which of the following statements is true?
options: The mask can be associated with a "subneted" class B address
The mask is definitely associated with a "subneted" class A address
The mask cannot be associated with a class C address
questions.hint: This mask can be used for a subneted class B address.

questions.text: A Go-Back-N protocol with a transmission window of size Wt
options: It can only work using a number of numbering bits greater than or equal to log2(Wt)
It can only work using a number of numbering bits greater than or equal to log2(Wt-1)
It can only work using a number of numbering bits greater than or equal to log2(Wt + 1)
questions.hint: Go-Back-N allows Wt <= 2^k-1, so k ≥ log2(Wt+1).

questions.text: ADSL (Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line) technology
options: It was mainly designed to provide a voice / data access service to a residential user mainly accessing the Web as a client
It was mainly designed to allow interconnection of local networks over large distances
It has been designed primarily to provide a purely data access service to web servers
questions.hint: See transparencies “ADSL”.

questions.text: The quality characteristics required by a telephony service are:
options: Transfer of information with a maximum delay of the order of hundreds of milliseconds and extremely low jitter; bit rate of the order of tens of kbit/s; probability of error not more than a few percent; probability of block not exceeding a few percent
Transfer of information with a maximum delay of the order of tens of seconds; negligible error and block probability
Transfer of information with a maximum delay of hundreds of milliseconds; bit rate of tens of Mbit/s; low error
questions.hint: See slides "Quality indices (telephony)".

questions.text: In the original IP routing, i.e., without the use of masks, the choice of the output interface on which to forward a packet is based
options: The full IP address subnet(net_id + host_id) of the recipient
On the network part subnet(net_id) of the recipient's IP address
Only on the host subnet(host_id) part of the recipient's IP address
questions.hint: Forwarding is based on net_id only.

questions.text: The DNS (Domain Name Service):
options: To increase reliability and responsiveness uses caches, but each resolution must reach authoritative server
Used by operators for sale of domain names
Based on hierarchical servers, each responsible for a zone
Product to distribute load on routers
questions.hint: DNS resolves host names using distributed hierarchical servers.

questions.text: Which of the following statements in the comparison between the Aloha and Slotted-Aloha protocols is false?
options: Slotted-Aloha allows a better exploitation of the capacity of the transmission medium
The performance of Aloha is less dependent than Slotted-Aloha on propagation delays
Aloha is simpler to implement by not requiring slot synchronization
questions.hint: Slotted-Aloha reduces partial collisions; Aloha simpler but more affected by delays.

questions.text: In the case of packet switching
options: The switching function allocates to the interlocutors a subset of network resources with which one or more circuits are established for connecting user terminals; the resources must be released if they are needed for establishing other circuits

The switching function allocates to the interlocutors in exclusive use a subset of network resources with which one or more circuits are established for connecting user terminals; the resources are released only at the end of communication

The switching function does not allocate to the interlocutors in exclusive use a subset of network resources; all network resources are always available for packet transmission; packets wait in appropriate queues until the necessary resources become available
questions.hint: See transparencies “Packet switching”.

questions.text: In the header (header) UDP, or in the PCI of the UDP protocol are mandatory contents
options: The TTL (Time To Live) field
The source and destination port
The source and destination IP address
questions.hint: See transparencies “UDP: segment header”.

questions.text: Internet routing tables
options: They indicate the sequence of routers to cross to reach a destination
They only indicate the next router to cross to reach the destination
They indicate the autonomous system sequence
questions.hint: See sheets “IP routing (next hop)”.

questions.text: Data transfer between two application processes in the OSI model occurs by involving
options: Only two entities of the application layer, one per system
At least one entity for each of the seven levels in both systems
An entity in each system, independent of the level
questions.hint: Transmitter passes all layers down; receiver goes up all layers.

questions.text: Consider two Ethernet LANs A and B, connected by a switch B1 and a router R1 (B1 and R1 are in parallel between the two LANs). Suppose that both the switch and router have all ports active and know all addresses (MAC and IP respectively) of hosts connected to the two LANs. When a host connected to LAN A transmits an ARP packet to obtain the MAC address of router R1, which of the following statements is true?
options: Forwarded on LAN B only by router R1
Forwarded on LAN B only by switch B1
The packet is forwarded on LAN B either by the switch or by the router, depending on the value of the destination MAC address contained in the packet
The packet is forwarded on LAN B by both router R1 and switch B1
questions.hint: Switch forwards broadcast to all ports; router responds only if target.

questions.text: The SMTP protocol
options: Operates on the UDP protocol, since email messages are usually short
Is based on messages that always include encrypted authentication
Is used for delivering outgoing email messages from a client to a given server
Is used to transfer email messages from a server to a client installed on a PC
questions.hint: SMTP sends messages from client to mail server.

questions.text: Using Stop-And-Wait on a non-sequential channel
options: Always handled without problems
Can cause protocol malfunctions and algorithm blocking
Can cause malfunctions but not blocking
questions.hint: With k=1, examples of blocking and information loss.

questions.text: An (N-1)-protocol allows interaction
options: Between (N+1) and (N-1)-entity
Between two (N-1)-entities
Between any two entities at different levels
Between two (N)-entities
questions.hint: Protocols work between same-layer entities.

questions.text: In the case of circuit switching:
options: The switching function allocates to the interlocutors a subset of network resources with which one or more circuits are established for connecting user terminals; the resources must be released if they are needed for establishing other circuits

The switching function allocates to the interlocutors in exclusive use a subset of network resources with which one or more circuits are established for connecting user terminals; the resources are released only at the end of communication

The switching function does not allocate to the interlocutors in exclusive use a subset of network resources; all network resources are always available for packet transmission; packets wait in appropriate queues until the necessary resources become available
questions.hint: See transparencies “Switching to circuit”.

questions.text: Version 4 IP addresses of class C characterize:
options: Multicast communications
Few networks with many hosts
Many networks with a small number of hosts
questions.hint: Class C addresses: many networks, few hosts.

questions.text: The CSMA and CSMA-CD protocols
options: Try to avoid interference between transmissions of users sharing a broadcast channel through preventive listening to the channel state; transmission can begin only if the channel is heard free

Do not implement any preventive control to avoid interference between transmissions of users sharing a broadcast channel; only in case of interference (collision) is action taken, repeating the transmission after a random delay
Try to avoid interference between transmissions of users sharing a broadcast channel through preventive listening to the channel state; transmission can begin only if the channel is actually free
questions.hint: Preventive listening reduces collisions.

questions.text: By signaling is meant
options: The transfer of information from one point to one or more other points
The exchange of information concerning the control of a telecommunications network
questions.hint: Reporting refers to signaling/control exchange.

questions.text: The MIME protocol allows
options: To have data encoded differently within the e-mail message
To reserve the resources on the network so that an email message with a multimedia file attached can reach the destination with guaranteed quality
To transmit useful information to the recipients of the e-mail to monitor the quality of the transmission
Check the playback of a multimedia file downloaded from the network
questions.hint: See slides “Message format: multimedia extensions”.

questions.text: Statistical multiplexing means
options: A fixed frequency multiplexing scheme in which the band assigned to the different information flows it is proportional to the transmission speed
A multiplexing scheme that provides for a random choice between frequency multiplexing and multiplexing over time
A multiplexing scheme that does not foresee a predetermined allocation of resources transmissive to information flows
questions.hint: The C corresponds to the definition of statistical multiplexing.

questions.text: What is the order of magnitude of the maximum transmission speed on an optical fiber?
options: 1 Tbit / s
1 kbit / s
1 Mbit / s
1 Gbit / s
1 bit / s
questions.hint: See transparencies “The optical fiber”.

questions.text: If a router receives a correct TCP packet, encapsulated in an IP packet with header destined for a non-existent TCP port (for which no application process is waiting):
options: Discard it and send an ICMP packet to the destination
Pass it to a default application process that handles all TCP packets for which no there is an application process available
Ignore the TCP port value and send the packet
Discard it and send an ICMP packet to the source
questions.hint: Since the TCP packet is encapsulated in an IP packet, the latter will not be able to detect the TCP port error, so the correct answer is C.

questions.text: The increment of the current window of the TCP transmitter
options: It is regulated only by the receiver
It is regulated only by the slow-start congestion control phase
It is regulated by the congestion control phase called slow-start and congestion avoidance
questions.hint: See “TCP congestion control” slides.

questions.text: The CSMA and CSMA-CD protocols admit 1-persistent and non-persistent versions
options: In the case of the 1-persistent version, if listening to the channel indicates that it is busy, the attempt is proposed for a random delay; in the case of non-persistent versions, if listening to the channel indicates that it is busy, the transmission starts as soon as the current transmission ends

In the case of the non-persistent version, if listening to the channel indicates that it is busy, the attempt is proposed for a random delay; in the case of 1-persistent versions, if listening to the channel indicates that it is busy, the transmission begins as soon as the current transmission ends
In both cases, if listening to the channel indicates that it is busy, the transmission attempt it is postponed with a random delay
questions.hint: See slides "CSMA".

questions.text: Suppose that between a transmitter and a receiver they implement an ARQ scheme (Automatic repeat request) of the Go-Back-N type the time that elapses between the start of the transmission of a data unit and the end of receipt of the corresponding acknowledgment is constant and greater than the time necessary to transmit the information that can be stored in the transmission window. In this situation, the increase of the transmission speed on the channels that connect the transmitter to the receiver
options: It decreases the amount of information transferred on average in the unit of time between the transmitter and the receiver
It fails to increase the amount of information transferred on average in the unit of time between transmitter and receiver
Increases the amount of information transferred on average in the unit of time between the transmitter and the receiver
questions.hint: n = Wt / (1 + 2 (Tp / Tx)) => at higher speeds, Tx decreases and n (efficiency) increases.

questions.text: In the OSI model, the delimitation of frames, ie the ability to identify on a channel the end of a packet, is a function:
options: Performed by all OSI levels
Typical of the level or sub-level adjacent to the physical level
Exclusive to the network level
questions.hint: Level 2 takes care of this.

questions.text: In the event of a loss of segments identified by receiving three hits, the current window size of the reno TCP transmitter
options: It is brought to half the size of the receiver window
It is brought back to the initial value, equal to one segment
It is placed in the middle of the current value (to be precise, in half of the current value plus a segment)
questions.hint: This is how TCP reno works.

questions.text: Frame Relay technology predicts
options: The transfer of fixed-size data units in non-connection-oriented mode
The transfer of data units of fixed size on virtual circuits
The transfer of data units of variable size on virtual circuits
questions.hint: See “Frame Relay” slides.

questions.text: The Network Address Translation (NAT) Mechanism
options: Realizes in OSI terms a mapping function
Can modify the IP addresses of the packets
Allows you to set the logical address of a host to the IP address
questions.hint: See slides "NAT".

questions.text: In the absence of other packets, the minimum time it takes for a packet to traverse the switch operating in store-and-forward mode
options: It grows as the packet transmission speed increases
It grows as the distance between the source and destination of the packet increases
It grows as the number of bits of which the packet is composed increases
questions.hint: See “Store and forward” slides.

questions.text: The PING application program
options: It uses ICMP protocol messages to determine the path followed to reach a host belonging to the internet
Use a TCP protocol option to check the connectivity of a host belonging to the network Internet
It uses ICMP protocol messages to check the connectivity of a host belonging to the network Internet
questions.hint: See transparencies of the “PING” command.

questions.text: A network topology with N nodes and M unidirectional channels is given. Each channel has capabilities C Mbit / s. The routing algorithm is such as to evenly distribute traffic over the network channels. The average number of channels traversed by a packet in the path from the source to the destination is equal to D. The maximum amount of traffic disposed of by the network increases if:
options: Decreases C to equal N, M and D.
Decreases M to equal N, D and C
Decreases D to equal N, M and C
Decreases N to equal D, M and C
questions.hint: if the average distance decreases, with the same channel capacity, the traffic disposed of should increase.

questions.text: Statistical multiplexing
options: Can only be used in connectionless networks
It is used in telephone networks because it is closely associated with the use of constant speed channels
It consists in sharing the same resource (transmission channel, memory device, etc.) by traffic sources that use it on an instantaneous need
Can only be used in connection oriented networks, but not circuit switched
questions.hint: By definition in statistical multiplexing the same resource can be used in frequency or in time to multiple sources.

questions.text: In a packet-switched network operating in store-and-forward mode, a larger data unit size
options: The routing complexity of each data unit increases
Increases the time that elapses from when a data unit reaches the input of a switch a when this leaves the switch
Increase the number of operations that must be performed by a switch to transfer the same total amount of user information
questions.hint: Long packets lead to a longer store time by the receiving node.

questions.text: Congestion control in the TCP protocol
options: It is not available
It is based on an autonomous decision by the transmitter based on any feedback (ACK) duplicates and on the expiry of the time-out
It is based on the signaling by the receiver of the available reception window
questions.hint: Per il controllo della congestione la CWND aumenta di 1 MSS per ogni ACK ricevuto finché non avviene un timeout.

questions.text: Window protocols are also called ARQ (Automatic Retransmission reQuest) because
options: In case of arrival of an incorrect packet, the receiver requests retransmission
If an ACK fails to return, the receiver requests retransmission
The expiration of the timeout at the transmitter corresponds to an automatic request for retransmission
questions.hint: see window protocols slide.

questions.text: In the case of common channel signaling
options: A signaling channel corresponds to each channel for the transfer of user information
A single signaling channel is used to control several transfer channels user information; the signaling channel operates in packet mode
A single signaling channel is used to control several transfer channels user information; the signaling channel operates in circuit mode
questions.hint: In common channel signaling, a single signaling channel operates in packet mode to control several user transfer channels.

questions.text: In the current state of technology, it is possible to transmit information without amplification along the transmission line over greater distances using
options: The Hertzian channel (radio, satellite)
Optical fibers
The twisted pairs
Coaxial cables
questions.hint: Radio/satellite channels allow for very long distances without intermediate amplification compared to physical cables.

questions.text: The (N + 1) -directory function associates
options: An (N + 1) -address to an (N) -address
A (N + 1) -title to an (N) -address
A (N + 1) -title to an (N + 2) -address
questions.hint: This follows the OSI naming conventions where titles are mapped to addresses of the layer below.

questions.text: The preamble prepended to IEEE 802.3 (Ethernet) data units is required for
options: Allow to keep the network synchronous
Allow the synchronization of repeaters and receivers encountered on the local network
Allow repeaters to retransmit data drives at the same rate at which they were received
questions.hint: The preamble provides a bit pattern for receiver clock synchronization.

questions.text: If a router detects an incorrect checksum on an IP packet, and therefore a potential error on the IP addresses contained in the packet, during the routing phase
options: Discard it and send an ICMP packet to the source only
It discards it and sends an ICMP packet to both the source and the destination
Discards it without reporting it to any other network entity
It still forwards it to the destination, however sending an ICMP packet to the source for report the error
questions.hint: If the header is corrupted (checksum error), the router cannot trust the source address to send an ICMP, so it just drops the packet.

questions.text: In the OSI model, which of the following functions is performed by session-level entities?
options: The routing of the data units in a type that is not completely connected
The choice of data representation syntax for a work session
The definition of synchronization points in a data unit stream
questions.hint: Session layer manages dialogue control and synchronization points.

questions.text: The complexity of the routing procedures used, within a node, for forwarding information has the greatest influence on the performance of a network in the case of
options: Packet switching without virtual circuits (datagram mode)
Packet switching with virtual circuits
Circuit switching
questions.hint: In datagram mode, every packet is routed independently, increasing per-packet processing overhead.

questions.text: The LLC SNaP (SubNetwork access Protocol) format of the IEEE 802.2 LLC protocol
options: Allows sharing of a broadcast transmission medium
Allows coexistence of a large number of protocols at levels higher than level
Is required in Internet for data unit transfer in subnets
Guarantees the recognition of transmission errors
questions.hint: SNAP allows multiplexing of various network layer protocols over LLC.

questions.text: In the CSMA and CSMA-CD protocol the concept of "persistence" refers to:
options: The way in which the transmission attempt occurs, if listening to the channel indicates that it is busy
The calculation of the time for which a station is authorized to occupy the channel
How the retransmission attempt occurs, if a collision has occurred
The time during which two transmissions overlap on the channel, which is a necessary condition for the collision to be detected
questions.hint: Persistence defines the behavior (wait or retry) when a node senses the medium is busy.

questions.text: In the IP header, or in the PCI of the IP protocol, they are contained:
options: The 16-bit Checksum field for checking the correctness of the header and of the data contained in the package
The Sequence Number field for numbering the segments
The Identification 3e Fragment Offset fields that allow the management of the fragmentation of packages
questions.hint: IP header contains fields specifically for fragmentation; checksum only covers the header, not data.

questions.text: Why does VDSL technology have high performance only if the distance between the cab of road and user's home is less than a hundred meters?:
options: Because the end-to-end delay between the user's home and the operator's control panel is reduced
Because the costs of laying cables are reduced
Because the shorter length of the copper cable allows the use of higher bit rate modulation
Because the connections have to cross fewer intermediate nodes
questions.hint: High-frequency signals used in VDSL attenuate quickly over copper, requiring short distances.

questions.text: Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) does not use address fields because
options: Take advantage of the underlying MAC addresses
Take advantage of top-level addresses
It must operate on point-to-point connections
It has no space in the plot header
questions.hint: In a direct point-to-point link, there is only one possible recipient, so addressing is redundant.

questions.text: The DHCP protocol provides that
options: A client uses an IP address as soon as it receives it from the server in a DHCP offer message.
A client may disconnect from the network without communicating it to the server.
If a server exists, it is unique on the client's local network.
The server never also provides the IP address of a DNS server in its response.
questions.hint: Clients can simply leave; DHCP leases eventually expire if not renewed.

questions.text: The fundamental functions of the link layer in the OSI model are
options: Flow control and recovery of transmission errors
Data drive routing
Transfer of binary digits on the channel
questions.hint: Error detection/recovery and flow control are core Layer 2 functions.

questions.text: During the slow-start phase of the TCP congestion control, the window transmitter current
options: It is halved for each missing ACK
It grows by one segment for each acknowledgment (ACK) received
Double for each acknowledgment (ACK) received
It remains constant over time
questions.hint: In slow start, the congestion window increases by 1 MSS for every ACK, effectively doubling every RTT.

questions.text: What is the order of magnitude of the maximum transmission rate on coaxial cable?
options: 1 Tbit / s
1 Mbit / s
1 bit / s
1 kbit / s
1 Gbit / s
questions.hint: Standard coaxial typically operates in the range of hundreds of Mbps.

questions.text: Window protocols can be used
options: Only for communications that use a connection
Both for communications that use a connection and for those that don't
Only for communications that do not use a connection
questions.hint: Windowing requires state synchronization (sequence numbers/ACKs), typical of connection-oriented services.

questions.text: The Address Resolution Protocol (ARP)
options: Obtain an Ethernet address to assign to the machine card it has made the ARP request
It allows a host to know the IP address of its DNS server
Realizes in OSI terms a mapping (translation) function between (3)-addresses and (2)-address
questions.hint: ARP maps Layer 3 (IP) addresses to Layer 2 (MAC) addresses.

questions.text: In the OSI model, the segmentation performed by a level entity (N + 1)
options: Create many (N + 1)-PDUs from a single (N + 1)-SDU
Create a (N + 1)-PDU from many (N)-SDUs
It combines many (N + 1)-PDUs in a single (N)-SDU
Create many (N + 1)-PCI for the same (N + 1)-PDU
questions.hint: Segmentation breaks down a larger service data unit into multiple protocol data units.

questions.text: Let Wt and Wr be the dimensions, respectively, of the transmission window and of the receive windows in a windowed protocol. Also let N be the total quantity of sequence numbers available to distinguish data drives. Which of the following constraints is a necessary and sufficient condition to avoid malfunctions on a channel that does not reverse the order of the data units?
options: N = Wt + 1
N = (Wt + Wr) / 2
N = Wr + 1
N >= Wt + Wr
questions.hint: The range of sequence numbers must be at least the sum of the sender and receiver windows to prevent overlap issues.

questions.text: The three fundamental elements that define a protocol are:
options: Algorithms, formats, timings
Syntax, semantics, timing
Algorithms, services, timing
Algorithms, formats, entities
questions.hint: Review the concepts related to General Networking.

questions.text: An Ethernet card of a Bridge (ie it reads and decides if and how to route)
options: All packets, regardless of the destination address
Only packets with a unicast destination MAC address equal to that of the bridge
Packets with broadcast destination MAC address only
Packets with multicast destination MAC address only
questions.hint: By definition a Bridge's ethernet reads and routes all packets.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is false?
options: An IP router can use the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) to know the MAC address of the router or host to which it is to deliver an IP packet
A host can use ICMP messages to verify another host's connectivity to the network Internet.
An IP router, which does not perform a NAT (Network Address Translator) function, does not modify the IP addresses of the packets to be re-transmitted
An IP host always only makes direct deliveries
questions.hint: A, B and C are correct as the ARP definitions are ICMP and NAT. By exclusion the answer is the D.

questions.text: To avoid blocking or loss of data units in a windowed protocol due to channels non-sequential, it is useful
options: Number the PDUs on a number of bits greater than 1 and do not limit the life time of the PDUs in the net
Number the PDUs on a number of bits greater than 1 and limit the life time of the PDUs in the network
Number the PDUs on a single bit and limit the life time of the PDUs in the network
questions.hint: By definition, in window protocols, PDUs must be numbered on a number of bits greater than 1. It is necessary that the packets have a minimum life time (Time to Live) otherwise it would lead to congestion of the intermediate nodes.

questions.text: The constraints on the maximum extension of an IEEE 802.3 local network (CSMA / CD) arise
options: Both from the propagation delay of the signals from one end of the network to the other, and from the attenuation of the signals on the transmission media.
Both from the attenuation of the signals on the transmission media and from the maximum delays tolerated by the users MAC service
By the number of bits that would be needed to increase the data units in the case of large delays propagation
questions.hint: Collision detection requires that the transmission time is at least twice the propagation delay.

questions.text: In the case where a windowed protocol is used on a channel that does not allow inversions in the sequence order of transmitted data units (that is on sequential channel), assuming to use a non-cyclic progressive numbering, the transmission and reception windows can never be in the following situation:
options: No sequence number included in the receive window is also included in the trasmission windows
The smallest sequence number in the transmission window is smaller than the smallest sequence number in the receiving window
The smallest sequence number in the receive window is smaller than the smallest number of sequence in the transmission window.
The largest sequence number in the receive window is larger than the largest number of sequence in the transmission window
questions.hint: The send window can advance only after receiving ACKs which must be sent by the receiver after the receiving a packet, but receiving it would necessarily involve a slide forward of the receiver.

questions.text: Medium Access Control (MAC) sublevel protocols serve purpose
options: To allow the sharing of a broadcast channel by means of a distributed algorithm
To allow the sharing of a broadcast channel through a centralized algorithm
To allow the sharing of a point-to-point channel
questions.hint: In the MAC sub-level the random access protocols (Aloha, CSMA, etc.) use distributed algorithms.

questions.text: The IEEE 802.3 standard (CSMA / CD) provides data units (also including layer 2)
options: Variable in size between 10 and 4500 octets
Variable in size between 64 and 1518 octets
Fixed size of 53
questions.hint: Review the concepts related to Data Link Layer & LANs.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true?
options: In the commercial standard Ethernet (CSMA / CD access protocols), one is defined minimum packet size to ensure correct collision identification
In the commercial standard Ethernet (CSMA / CD access protocol), one is defined minimum packet size to distinguish packets from IEEE 802.3 standard packets

In the commercial standard Ethernet (CSMA / CD access protocol), one is defined minimum packet size to ensure better performance, in terms of traffic disposed of, al access protocol compared to what you would have with maximum size packets
questions.hint: On ethernet the collision detection is a function of the length of the packet and the network extension.

questions.text: In the header (header) TCP, or in the PCI of the TCP protocol, they are mandatory content
options: The TTL (Time To Live) field that allows the elimination from the network of packets that have too many routers went through
The sequence number and the ack number, for the numbering of the segment and the acknowledgments (ACK)
The fragmentation field for managing segment fragmentation
questions.hint: See TCP slides for sequence and acknowledgement number fields.

questions.text: A protocol
options: It is a set of semantic and syntactic rules to allow communication between two entities equal level
It is a set of semantic and syntactic rules to allow communication between two entities same system
It is a set of semantic and syntactic rules to allow communication between two systems which are linked together
It is a set of semantic and syntactic rules to allow communication between two entities different systems
questions.hint: By definition, an entity communicates with other peer entities (same level).

questions.text: In a Store-and-Forward packet network, increasing the number of nodes between source and destination
options: It leads to an increase in the delivery time, directly proportional to the size of the package
It leads to an increase in delivery time, directly proportional to the average speed of the channels
It leads to an increase in the delivery time, inversely proportional to the size of the package
questions.hint: Each node must store the entire packet before forwarding, adding a delay proportional to the packet size at each hop.

questions.text: The UDP protocol provides a service
options: Unreliable (i.e. no delivery guarantee) and connectionless
Reliable (i.e. with delivery guarantee) and connectionless
Unreliable (i.e. without delivery guarantee) and connection oriented
questions.hint: UDP implements simple, unreliable connectionless multiplexing.

questions.text: The TCP protocol provides a service
options: Unreliable (i.e. no delivery guarantee) and connectionless
Reliable (i.e. with delivery guarantee) and connectionless
Unreliable (i.e. without delivery guarantee) and connection oriented
Reliable (i.e. with delivery guarantee) and connection oriented
questions.hint: TCP provides reliable, connection-oriented data transfer with flow and congestion control.

questions.text: The PPP (Point-to-point-Protocol)
options: Use the byte-stuffing technique to ensure data transparency
Use the bit-stuffing technique to ensure data transparency
Does not guarantee the transparency of data
questions.hint: PPP uses a special flag byte and escapes it via byte-stuffing.

questions.text: Comparing Fast Ethernet at 100 Mb / s (100Base T) with Ethernet at 10 Mb / s, which of the following statements is false?
options: The distance constraints between the nodes are more stringent
A different access protocol is used
A different physical layer is used
questions.hint: Both use the same CSMA/CD access protocol.

questions.text: Which of the following protocols does not perform error detection functions on data drives?
options: LaPB (Link access Protocol Balanced)
IEEE 802.2 LLC (Logical Link Protocol)
PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol)
LaPF (Link access Procedure to Frame-mode bearer services)
questions.hint: LLC (specifically Type 1) does not perform error control.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true?
options: A T1 topology, with N nodes, C channels and M1 average distance, always allows one to be disposed of lower amount of traffic of a T2 topology, with N nodes, C channels and average distance M2> M1, only with traffic evenly distributed between nodes.

A T1 topology, with N nodes, C channels and M1 average distance, always allows one to be disposed of traffic quantity lower than a T2 topology, with N nodes, C channels and average distance M2> M1, regardless of the traffic distribution.

The amount of traffic disposed of in a T1 topology, with N nodes, C channels and average distance M1, with respect to to that disposed of in a T2 topology, with N nodes, C channels and average distance M2> M1, depends on the traffic distribution between nodes
questions.hint: Network performance depends heavily on the specific traffic matrix and distribution.

questions.text: The main differences between a Frame Relay network and an Internet IP network are possible include:
options: The use or non-use of aRQ (automatic Retransmission reQuest) techniques in each section of the network
The transfer of information in connection-oriented rather than non-connection-oriented mode connection
Transfer of data units of variable size instead of fixed size
questions.hint: Frame relay is connection-oriented (virtual circuits), IP is connectionless (datagrams).

questions.text: Consider an Ethernet LAN with 10 nodes. Partition the network into two networks interconnected by transparent bridges. Which of the following statements is false?
options: The bridge separates the collision domains of the two interconnected networks
The performance of the network in terms of traffic disposed improves in any traffic condition, that is, completely independent of the distribution of traffic between nodes
The bridge introduces an additional delay in transmissions between bridged nodes
It is not necessary to change the configuration of the nodes connected to the LAN to allow a correct operation after partitioning the network
questions.hint: If all traffic is inter-segment, performance might not improve due to bridge processing.

questions.text: Consider two LANs (Ethernet 10BaSE) A and B, connected by a bridge B1 and by a router R1 (B1 and R1 are in parallel between the two LANs). Suppose the bridge and router have both ports active and know all the addresses (MAC and IP respectively) of the hosts connected to two LANs. When a host connected to LAN A transmits an IP packet to a host connected to the LAN B
options: The packet is forwarded over LAN B either by the bridge or by the router, depending on the address value Destination MAC contained in the packet
The packet is forwarded on LAN B by both router R1 and bridge B1
The packet is forwarded on LAN B only by router R1
The packet is forwarded on LAN B only by bridge B1
questions.hint: Review the concepts related to Transport Layer.

questions.text: The size of the current TCP transmitter window during a connection
options: It is regulated exclusively on the basis of the notification by the receiver of the size of the receiving window to perform flow control
It varies with congestion in the network and due to the flow control exercised by the receiver
It is fixed
questions.hint: The sender window is the minimum between the congestion window (cwnd) and the receiver's advertised window (rwnd).

questions.text: In the event of a segment loss identified by receiving three hits, the size of the current TCP transmitter window
options: It is brought to a value equal to half of the threshold
It is brought to a value equal to the threshold value
It is returned to the initial value, equal to one segment
questions.hint: This refers to the Fast Recovery mechanism in TCP Reno.

questions.text: What is the order of magnitude of the maximum transmission rate on a twisted pair?
options: 1 Tbit / s
1 kbit / s
1 Mbit / s
1 Gbit / s
1 bit / s
questions.hint: Modern twisted pair (e.g., Cat6e) supports Gbit speeds.

questions.text: An IP router
options: It performs both fragmentation and reassembly of the datagram
Performs fragmentation of datagrams, but not reassembly
It does not perform datagram fragmentation
Performs fragmentation of datagrams, and reassembly only if an appropriate bit is set in the IP header
questions.hint: Reassembly is only done by the destination host.

questions.text: Common channel signaling
options: It requires the use of signaling messages that contain the identifier of the connection to which they refer to
It is only used in packet-switched networks, because in circuit, the associated channel signaling technique is used
It cannot be used in cell or packet switched networks because it is too difficult identify connections in these networks without associating them with a signaling channel
It makes use of common transmission channels that are associated with each connection being made opening the connection itself
questions.hint: Common channel signaling uses a separate packet network for control messages.

questions.text: Code division multiplexing
options: it is a special case of time division only
it is a special case of frequency division only
it allows to use multiplexing and switching on the same physical medium
it does not necessarily need to be coupled to time or frequency multiplexing
questions.hint: CDMA is based on orthogonal codes, independent of time/frequency slots.

questions.text: An (N) -protocol regulates interactions
options: between an (N) -entity and a (N-1) -SAP
between (N) -entities of the same system or of different systems
between an (N) -entity and all entities below it in the protocol stack
between an (N) -entity and the (N-1) -entity
questions.hint: Protocols define rules between peer entities.

questions.text: A Go-Back-N window protocol provides that:
options: when a packet is received with an error, the last N data units are retransmitted
the transmitter receives feedback for the last N data units transmitted before it can start transmission of other data units
the transmitter cannot send more than N data units before having received one or more acknowledgments
every time a time-out expires, the data unit whose sequence order is equal to is retransmitted sequence number of the last transmitted data unit decreased by N
questions.hint: The window size N limits the number of unacknowledged packets.

questions.text: Which of these HTTP statements is false?
options: HTTP is an application-level protocol that allows you to transfer objects on a web page
HTTP is a language that allows you to define the format of Web pages
HTTP is based on a client-server architecture
Without additional workarounds, HTTP is a stateless type protocol
questions.hint: HTML is the language for defining format; HTTP is the transfer protocol.

questions.text: Using the piggybacking technique in window protocols the advantage of:
options: Confirm the receipt of more than one data unit through a single acknowledgment
Transmit data units even outside the transmission window
Increase the likelihood that an ACK will be received by the transmitter
Reduce the percentage of control information that is carried over the network
questions.hint: Piggybacking sends ACKs inside data packets, reducing overhead.

questions.text: The DHCP discover message is sent over UDP using as the IP destination address:
options: The limited broadcast IP address 255.255.255.255
The loopback address 127.0.0.1
The IP address of the local DNS servers
The IP address of the DHCP servers on the local network
questions.hint: Review the concepts related to Application Layer.

questions.text: What disadvantage does datagram packet switching present compared to circuit switching?
options: Calculation of the routing to the source
Variability of data delays
Routing calculation at communication opening
High communication opening time
questions.hint: Datagram switching introduces jitter (variable delay) due to independent routing.

questions.text: In the absence of errors, the efficiency of a Stop and Wait protocol:
options: it is always higher than the efficiency of a Go-Back-N protocol

it is less than the efficiency of a Go-Back-N protocol only if the transmission time of a packet plus the round trip time on the channel is less than the time it takes to send the entire window transmission of the Stop and Wait protocol
it is less than the efficiency of a Go-Back-N protocol only if the transmission time of a packet is greater than the round trip propagation time on the channel
it is always less than the efficiency of a Go-Back-N protocol
questions.hint: Stop and Wait is a Go-Back-N with window size 1; if N > 1, Go-Back-N is more efficient.

questions.text: What is the playout buffer for?
options: To avoid situations of congestion on the network
Access multimedia content faster thanks to local caching
To compensate for network delays in streaming multimedia content
To manage the retransmission window for multimedia contents
questions.hint: Playout buffers smooth out jitter in streaming.

questions.text: In a virtual circuit packet-switched network the number of labels used for routing it is proportional:
options: To the number of possible destinations
At the average number of channels outgoing from each node
The number of active connections
At the average number of nodes to cross
questions.hint: Review the concepts related to Transport Layer.

questions.text: How are ARP messages encapsulated?
options: In the body of an HTTP message
Directly in an Ethernet frame
In one or more TCP segments
Directly in an IP datagram
questions.hint: ARP is a Layer 2 protocol that doesn't use IP headers.

questions.text: What happens when the transmission timeout in TCP is set to a value significantly less than the round-trip time?
options: The time it takes to recover from segment loss situations is getting longer
Unnecessary segment retransmissions may occur
There is never any visible effect
The receiver no longer guarantees that correct data is supplied to the process listening on the socket
questions.hint: Early timeouts trigger retransmissions of packets that are still in flight.

questions.text: The instability of the Aloha and Slotted Aloha protocols is caused by:
options: The increase in propagation delay when the traffic offered exceeds a certain threshold
The decrease in traffic disposed of when the traffic offered exceeds a certain threshold
The increase in traffic disposed of when the offered traffic exceeds a certain threshold
questions.hint: High traffic leads to more collisions, reducing successful throughput.

questions.text: Consider a host that is transmitting data using the TCP protocol. Given a transmitter current window of size equal to 10 segments, with a maximum receiver window equal to 40 segments, when the transmitter receives a segment containing an ACK from the side of the receiver, which of the following situations is impossible?
options: The transmitter's current window becomes 1 segment
The transmitter's current window becomes 51 segments
The current window at the transmitter becomes equal to 9 segments
The current window at the transmitter becomes equal to 5 segments
questions.hint: The sender window cannot exceed the receiver's advertised window (40 segments in this case).

questions.text: Which of these fields is not contained in the header of an IPv4 datagram?
options: Destination IP address
Time to live (TTL)
Protocol
Destination port
questions.hint: The destination port is a field belonging to the transport layer (TCP/UDP), not the network layer (IP).

questions.text: In the hierarchy provided by the DNS for the resolution of names not present in the cache, which one level is located immediately below the Root DNS Server?
options: Top-level domain (TLD) DNS server
Local DHCP servers
Local DNS server
Authoritative DNS servers
questions.hint: The DNS hierarchy starts at Root, followed by TLD servers (.com, .org, .it), then Authoritative servers.

questions.text: The current congestion window at the TCP transmitter at the start of the connection:
options: It has a size negotiated with the receiver and equal to half the window of the receiver
It has a size equal to a segment of maximum size (MSS)
It has a size negotiated with the receiver and equal to the maximum value of the receiver window
It has a random size chosen during the opening phase of the connection
questions.hint: At the start of a connection (Slow Start phase), the cwnd is initialized to 1 MSS.

questions.text: In a packet-switched network operating in store-and-forward mode a smaller size of data units:
options: Decreases the number of operations that must be performed by a switch to transfer the same total amount of user information
The probability of losing the packet increases with the same probability of error on the bit
The routing complexity of each data unit decreases
Decreases the time from when a data unit reaches the input of a switch until it leaves the switch
questions.hint: Smaller packets require less time to be fully received (stored) before the forwarding process can begin.

questions.text: In a one-way ring topology, with 10 nodes and uniform unicast traffic (all nodes transmit the same amount of traffic to all others), the average number of channels traversed by a package is equal to:
questions.hint: In a unidirectional ring of N nodes, the average distance is (N-1)/2. For N=10, it's 4.5, which rounds to 5 in this context.

questions.text: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) congestion control is based on:
options: On the variation of the number of parity bits inserted in the transmitted segments
On the trend of the size of the segments transmitted to the state of the network
About adapting the transmitter window to the receiver's memory availability
On the dynamics of the transmitter window size
questions.hint: Congestion control adjusts the congestion window (cwnd) based on perceived network loss or delay.

questions.text: The minimum time required to send a 100Kbyte packet between two stations separated by 300 meters, using a wired network with UTP (Unshielded Twisted Pair) and crossing 3 interconnection equipment operating in store and forward mode, is of the order of:
options: A few seconds
It can only be calculated by knowing the transmission bit rate on the channels
A few milliseconds
Hundreds of milliseconds
questions.hint: Without the transmission rate (bandwidth), the serialization delay (the dominant factor) cannot be determined.

questions.text: What are the source and destination port fields in TCP and UDP for?
options: To implement a multiplexing / demultiplexing mechanism for processes on hosts
To manage the allocation of resources on the router on the path from source to destination
To indicate the network interfaces on which packets will be forwarded by IP
To indicate the physical interfaces on which the frames will be transmitted by Ethernet
questions.hint: Ports allow the transport layer to direct data to the specific application process (socket) on a host.

questions.text: Among the fundamental functions of the transport layer in the OSI model we find:
options: Exchange of labels in circuit switching
Reading data from a terminal device
Recovery of transmission errors
Data drive routing
questions.hint: The transport layer (like TCP) provides end-to-end error recovery and reliability.

questions.text: At the same rate of information transmitted, which of the following line codings it requires a physically lower bitrate?
options: 12B15B encoding
4B5B encoding
They all require the same bit rate
8B10B encoding
questions.hint: If the "rate of information transmitted" refers to the effective bit rate, the physical line rate adapts to the overhead of each specific encoding.

questions.text: If a router receives an IP packet, with correct checksum, with source IP address and destination equal and TTL field = 9
options: It routes it to the destination
It still forwards it to the destination, however sending an ICMP packet to the source for report the error
It discards it and sends an ICMP error packet to the source
Discard the package
questions.hint: While unusual, an IP packet with the same source/destination is valid (loopback or local delivery) as long as the checksum and TTL are valid.

questions.text: The preamble in the Ethernet packet:
options: It allows to recognize transmission errors
Used to identify the type of protocol transported in the data field of the Ethernet packet
It allows you to identify the application process to which to deliver the package
It is necessary to allow the receiver node to tune its clock with the clock of the transmitter node
questions.hint: The preamble provides a bit pattern for clock synchronization between transmitter and receiver.

options: They have no valid IP addresses
They can exchange IP packets directly
They can only exchange IP packets via a router
They cannot exchange IP packets
questions.hint: Since they share the same subnet prefix (/24), they are on the same local network and can communicate directly.

questions.text: The protocol SMTP
options: it is used by a mail client to get a mail message from a server
allows a mail server to tell another mail server who the sender of a mail server is message
allows a mail server to verify the identity of a user who wants to send a message
it is based on the telnet protocol
questions.hint: SMTP is used for "pushing" mail from client to server or between servers.

questions.text: TCP messages contain a sequence number indicating
options: the next byte the receiver expects to receive
the message number in the sequence of messages transmitted over the TCP connection
the sequence number of the message in a set of fragments produced by fragmenting a bigger message
the position of the first byte of the message in the sequence of bytes transmitted on the TCP connection
questions.hint: TCP sequence numbers track bytes, not packets, identifying the position of the first byte in the stream.

questions.text: Congestion control in TCP
options: imposes a maximum number of TCP connections that a station can open
is based on information received from routers present on the path
is present only for some types of connection
limits the size of the transmission window
questions.hint: Congestion control effectively caps the window size to match network capacity.

questions.text: In the WI-FI protocol with DCF and handshaking
options: sending the RTS and CTS packets reduces the probability of collisions on the data packets
collisions are completely avoided thanks to the carrier sense mechanism
sending the RTS packets and the CTS allows two terminals, one of which is hidden, to send their plots at the same time
collisions on any type of data transmitted are completely avoided
questions.hint: The RTS/CTS mechanism addresses the "hidden node" problem, reducing collisions on large data frames.

questions.text: The HEAD method of the HTTP protocol is used to:
options: get the header of a web page
send only the header of an HTTP request
change the header, or home page, of a web server
receive only the HTTP response header
questions.hint: HEAD requests the same response as GET but without the message body.

questions.text: The receipt on node A of an ICMP Echo Reply packet sent by node B indicates that
options: A and B are able to exchange IP packets
A is able to send IP packets to B but not vice versa
B is able to send IP packets to A but not vice versa
B is able to send IP packets to A but vice versa is not guaranteed
questions.hint: An Echo Reply proves that the request reached B and the response reached A.

questions.text: The ARP Request frame is used for learning
options: the MAC address of a station connected to an IP network other than that of the source
the IP address of an Ethernet node directly connected to the source node
the IP address of a station given its internet name
the MAC address of an IP node directly connected to the source node
questions.hint: ARP resolves a known IP address to a MAC address on the same local segment.

questions.text: The DHCP protocol
options: it is used for automatic configuration of an IP station
it only provides IP stations with private type addresses
provides the stations with the IP address corresponding to a given domain name
it does not allow a station to reuse the same IP address already used during a previous connection to the local network
questions.hint: DHCP assigns IP addresses, masks, gateways, and DNS server info automatically.

questions.text: Given a topology (nodes, channels and associated costs), the optimal path between a source and a destination
options: it never changes even if a channel becomes unavailable
it changes depending on the node running the link state algorithm
it is the same whether a link state algorithm is used or a distance vector algorithm is used
it never changes even if the cost of the channels changes
questions.hint: Both algorithms are designed to find the shortest path based on the same metrics; they just use different methods.

questions.text: When an Ethernet switch receives an ARP Request packet
options: it only forwards it to the port to which the network's DHCP server is connected
forwards it on all ports except the one from which the packet was received
it forwards it only on ports on which multicast traffic has been enabled
it only forwards it on the port to which the destination node / host is connected
questions.hint: ARP Requests are broadcast at the MAC layer; a switch floods broadcast frames to all ports except the source.

questions.text: IP version 4 addresses are:
options: randomly assigned to the various stations connected to the internet, regardless of theirs position
assigned by the manufacturers of the network cards
